scope: data-rates: factual consistency of every number and claim on the live roscap.co.uk pages and in homepage concepts D, E and F; fact-check of the market rates as of 31 October 2026 against the concept values, the earlier video frames, the live homepage rates section and the feed JSON; assessment of the live rates feed (semantics, robustness, licensing) with recommendations only.
summary: The deal data is in good shape: all 22 cards on /track-record match deals.json on city, amount, product, asset and capital, and the deals-data embedded in concepts D, E and F is byte-identical to deals.json; the only differences are label wording (p.a. versus Rate p.a., a hyphen in the Dublin card). The headline statistics (60+, £120m+, 25+) are identical on the live page and in the concepts and are not contradicted by the listed deals, but the concepts' call to action View all 22 transactions contradicts both 60+ projects funded and the track record's own Selected Transactions framing. The market-rate values are right everywhere (BoE 3.75%, Fed 3.75% to 4.00%, Euribor 3M 2.643% for the 29 October fixing) and the concept panel was fully correct for 28 October; what is wrong is the movement labelling: the live tooltips describe a December 2025 cut as the last Bank of England decision, date the Fed decision one day late, and give the current fixing date as the previous one, and the earlier video frames repeat the same two errors. The feed cannot yet produce the approved Held, date decision labels because it only records the size and date of the last change, not the last decision. The feed also wrote 400.00% - 400.00% for the Fed on 21 October for about 12 hours because FRED returned HTML and nothing validates values. Displaying Euribor on a commercial site without an EMMI licence is an open legal point that the feed's own README flags and that Clemente must decide. Direct fetches of bankofengland.co.uk, federalreserve.gov, emmi-benchmarks.eu, fred.stlouisfed.org and euribor-rates.eu were blocked in this session, so primary pages were corroborated through web search results and the feed's own history rather than read directly.
strengths: All 22 deals on /track-record match deals.json exactly on city, amount, product, asset class and capital provider; the deals-data JSON embedded in concepts D, E and F is identical to deals.json (22 records, same order).

The stat tiles 60+, £120m+ and 25+ are identical on the live home page (data-count 60/120/25) and in all three concepts; the £120m+ figure is consistent with the listed deals once EUR and USD deals are converted (about £142m to £144m including Tirana, about £127m to £129m excluding it).

Every rate value in the concept panel was correct for 28 October 2026: 3.75% held at the 17 Sep 2026 decision, 3.75% to 4.00% held at the 28 Oct 2026 decision, Euribor 3M 2.618% down 2.0 bps at the 27 Oct fixing. The BoE and Fed lines are still correct on 31 October.

The feed's Euribor history matches every fixing that could be verified independently (19 Oct 2.643, 20 Oct 2.646, 21 Oct 2.670, 22 Oct 2.677, 23 Oct 2.666, 26 Oct 2.638, 27 and 28 Oct 2.618), so its 29 Oct value of 2.643% (+2.5 bps) is credible.

The feed is well engineered for its size: standard-library script, keeps last good values and marks them stale, opens a GitHub issue and fails the run on a source outage, serves JSON with access-control-allow-origin: *, runs every 3 hours and commits only on change.

The concepts quietly fixed one absolute promise in the live copy: ensuring every client and project secures the most appropriate form of capital became so that each client secures the most suitable form of capital.
The footer disclaimer and /disclaimer state clearly that Roscap is not authorised or regulated by the FCA; the company number 13536901 on /disclaimer matches the brief.
The claim across the UK, Europe and North America is supported by the data: 16 UK deals, 5 in Europe (Albania, France, Ireland, Italy, Spain) and 1 in the USA, 7 countries in all.

findings.title: Euribor is displayed on a commercial site without an EMMI licence (owner decision needed)
findings.evidence: Live card EURIBOR 3-Month 2.643% +0.025% (rendered 31 Oct 2026, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sonar/6b47e843-950d-5a6c-8dda-ec854c8993c6/scratchpad/shots/data-rates/live-rates-section.png); feed source field: Euribor 3-month daily fixing, via euribor-rates.eu (a scrape of an HTML table on a third-party site run by Triami Media B.V.). EMMI's Euribor rates page states that delayed rates can be consulted free after registration with a 24-hour delay and may solely be used for non-commercial purposes, and that subscription is mandatory for any commercial use (https://www.emmi-benchmarks.eu/benchmarks/euribor/rate/ and https://www.emmi-benchmarks.eu/faq/subscriptions/). EMMI's 2021-2022 fee schedule listed a Delayed Data licence covering publication of delayed data on websites at 1,060 euro per hosted website per year (https://www.emmi-benchmarks.eu/globalassets/documents/pdf/communication/news/d0344a-2021-2022-fee-schedule.pdf); the 2024-2025 schedule says a licence is required to distribute delayed data (https://www.emmi-benchmarks.eu/globalassets/documents/pdf/subscriptions/d0196b-2024-2025-fee-schedule.pdf); the 2026-2027 schedule exists (https://www.emmi-benchmarks.eu/globalassets/documents/pdf/subscriptions/d0167a-2026---2027-fee-schedule.pdf) but could not be read because the host is blocked in this session. The feed's own README says: The organisation that publishes Euribor states that redisplaying it on a commercial site needs a licence. Many sites redisplay it regardless. Roscap's call, not a technical matter. The concept panel credits euribor-rates.eu, not EMMI, and omits the Euribor registered-trademark notice.
findings.recommendation: Put the choice to Clemente before the approved odometer panel ships: (a) keep Euribor and obtain EMMI's Delayed Data licence, then print Source: EMMI, Euribor is a registered trademark of the European Money Markets Institute, delayed data, under the panel; or (b) replace the third card with the ECB deposit facility rate (a policy rate like the other two, which also makes the Held, date decision chip apply to all three cards and removes the licensing question). Until decided, leave the live card as is but do not add Euribor to new pages.

findings.title: Live change figures and tooltips misdescribe what the numbers are
findings.evidence: Rendered with Playwright on 31 Oct 2026 about 01:20 UTC: #changerate-boe -0.25% with title Change at the last Bank of England decision (18 December 2025), but the last Bank of England decision was on 17 Sep 2026 and was a hold (6 to 3); the -0.25% is the December 2025 cut, ten months old. #changerate-fed +0.25% with title Change at the last Federal Reserve decision (17 September 2026), but the FOMC decision was announced on 16 Sep 2026 (17 Sep is the effective date in FRED series DFEDTARU) and the last decision was the 28 Oct 2026 hold. #changerate-euribor +0.025% with title Change since the previous daily fixing (29 October 2026), but 29 Oct is the date of the current fixing; the previous fixing was 28 Oct at 2.618%. The earlier video frames carry the same two errors: Raised 25 bps at the 17 Sep 2026 decision and 2.638% Down 2.8 bps since the 26 Oct fixing, where 2.638% is itself the 26 Oct fixing and the fall is measured from the 23 Oct fixing (2.666%). Source: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sonar/6b47e843-950d-5a6c-8dda-ec854c8993c6/scratchpad/shots/data-rates/live-rates-hover.png, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sonar/6b47e843-950d-5a6c-8dda-ec854c8993c6/scratchpad/video/sheet_03.png.
findings.recommendation: Until the approved panel replaces this section, edit the footer script (Home page settings, footer code) so the tooltips read: BoE and Fed: Last change: cut/raise of 0.25 pp on <changed_on>; rate held at the most recent decision; Euribor: Fixing of <as_of>; change on the previous fixing. Fix the Fed date by publishing a decision date from the feed (see DR-06) rather than FRED's effective date.

findings.title: Feed once published 400.00% - 400.00% for the Fed and nothing on the page would stop it happening again
findings.evidence: Repo history of rates.json (public repo edusancheez2005/roscap-rates, read-only clone): commits 84e9ded (21 Oct 2026 17:40 UTC) and 9d1bf7a (21:59 UTC) contain fed.display 400.00% - 400.00%, change_display 0.00% and changed_on equal to an HTML fragment (<link href=https://fonts.googleapis.com/css?family=Open+Sans:300 ...). FRED answered with an HTML page instead of CSV and fetch_rates.py parsed the first comma-separated token as a number. The next good commit is c9113bf at 05:23 UTC on 22 Oct, so the home page showed 400.00% - 400.00% for roughly 12 hours. fetch_rates.py has no range or format validation (rule in its docstring is only never write zeros) and the footer script prints rate.display verbatim.
findings.recommendation: Feed (recommendation only): in fetch_rates.py check that the FRED response's first line starts with DATE or observation_date, that every parsed value is a finite number between 0 and 25, and that every date matches YYYY-MM-DD; on any failure raise so the existing stale fallback keeps the last good value. Website: in the footer script skip a card when Number(rate.value) is not finite or is outside 0 to 25, leaving the Designer text in place, and log the reason.

findings.title: Static Designer fallback values are stale, unlabelled, and the stale flag is ignored
findings.evidence:
Static HTML in live/html/index.html:

2.642%

+0.006%

; 2.642% +0.006% is the feed's very first output on 17 Oct 2026 (the 16 Oct fixing). If fetch() fails the script only runs console.error and the page shows these numbers with no date. The script never reads data.stale or rate.stale, so a rate kept from a failed run would be shown as current.
findings.recommendation: In the Designer set the six placeholder texts to an en dash so nothing stale can show; in the footer script render the Updated line only after a successful fetch, and when data.stale includes a key append (last good value, source unavailable) to that card's tooltip and skip its change figure.

findings.title: Updated 31 October 2026 is the check time, not the data date
findings.evidence: Rendered line Updated 31 October 2026 (#rates-updated) sits under a Euribor value whose as_of is 2026-10-29 and a BoE value whose as_of the script sets to dt.date.today() rather than a data date; the Fed as_of is 2026-10-30. The feed defines updated as the oldest successful fetch time of the three.
findings.recommendation: Label the line Checked 31 Oct 2026 and show the data date in each card (29 Oct fixing, 28 Oct 2026 decision), as the approved panel already does. Feed: set boe.as_of to the date of the latest Bank Rate row rather than today, and add a per-rate published_at.

findings.title: The approved panel's Held, <date> decision labels cannot be generated from the current feed
findings.evidence: Concept F markup (lines 496 to 509): Held 17 Sep 2026 decision, Held 28 Oct 2026 decision, Down 2.0 bps 27 Oct 2026 fixing, all hard-coded; none of the three concept files calls fetch() (grep count 0). The feed exposes value, change (size of the last change), changed_on (date of the last change), as_of and change_basis only. It has no decision date, no decision outcome, no previous fixing date, and for Euribor changed_on duplicates as_of. With today's feed the only truthful BoE chip would be Cut 25 bps, 18 Dec 2025, which the owner has already rejected in favour of Held.
findings.recommendation: Feed repo (recommendations only, nothing changed): add per rate previous_value, previous_as_of, change_bps, last_change_on, last_change_bps, last_decision_date, last_decision_outcome (held, cut or raised), next_decision_date, move_display (Held, Down 2.0 bps) and move_note (17 Sep 2026 decision, 27 Oct 2026 fixing), plus a top-level schema_version. Drive the BoE and Fed decision dates from a small calendar.json in the repo holding the published MPC and FOMC dates for the current and next year (from bankofengland.co.uk and federalreserve.gov), refreshed once a year; outcome is held when the most recent past decision date is later than last_change_on. For Euribor set previous_as_of to the prior fixing's date. The Webflow panel then prints these strings and never computes copy itself.

findings.title: View all 22 transactions contradicts 60+ Projects funded and the track record's Selected Transactions framing
findings.evidence: Concept F line 540 and D/E equivalents: View all 22 transactions (link to /track-record). Same page, stat tile: 60+ Projects funded (data-count 60, identical on live). /track-record: Selected Transactions. The following examples highlight a selection of completed transactions arranged and advised by Roscap. Live /track-record has exactly 22 cards; the earlier video round also used 22 transactions across 7 countries. If 60+ projects were funded, 22 cannot be all of them.
findings.recommendation: Change the button to View 22 selected transactions (or See the full track record) in the approved concept F module; keep 60+ only if Clemente confirms the figure, otherwise use the number of transactions he can stand behind.

findings.title: Join hundreds of current partners is not supported by anything on the site
findings.evidence: Hero copy: Join hundreds of current partners who are successfully working with Roscap. The Our Partners section (.assets-card-grid) shows 8 logo images, all with alt="". Step 06: receive commissions in perpetuity. Both flagged as unconfirmed by the owner; no other page gives a partner count.
findings.recommendation: Ask Clemente for the real count; if it cannot be evidenced, use Join the partners already working with Roscap and keep the logo grid. Qualify step 06 as commissions on subsequent deals we complete with your client, under the partner agreement.

findings.title: Timescale promises in the FAQ
findings.evidence: FAQ: Roscap can secure bridging loans in as little as 5-10 working days, subject to valuation and legal readiness. Development finance and commercial mortgages typically complete within 6-8 weeks, depending on lender due diligence and asset complexity. Hard rule 1 asks for promises of timescales to be flagged; the as little as phrasing is a marketing promise even though both sentences are hedged.
findings.recommendation: Keep the hedges and reword to Bridging loans have completed in 5 to 10 working days where valuation and legals were ready; development finance and commercial mortgages typically take 6 to 8 weeks. Timings are indicative and depend on the lender, valuation and legal timetable.

findings.title: Mowgli Frere's title contradicts his bio
findings.evidence: Team card: Head of Southern Europe. Bio text: He is now the Head of Western Europe for Roscap, sourcing Real Estate opportunities. Both appear on the same page (live/html/about-us.html, one occurrence each).
findings.recommendation: Pick one title and update the Teams CMS item (role field and bio rich text) so both agree.

findings.title: Case-study figures in Insights do not line up with the track record
findings.evidence: Blog (1 Jul 2026): £2.665m bridging loan, 12-month facility, Recognise Bank, 65% LTV, development site in Burnage, Manchester, 66-home scheme. Track record Manchester card: £2.7m, Commercial Mortgage, Mixed-Use, Challenger Bank, 65% LTV, 6.90% p.a. Either a different deal (then the case study is missing from the track record) or the same deal described inconsistently. Separately, the Financing Social Housing post says Roscap has arranged over £20 million of social and supported housing finance, while the track record lists one social housing deal (Wakefield, £4.2m).
findings.recommendation: Confirm with Clemente. If different deals, add the Manchester bridging loan as a 23rd track record card (and to deals.json) and link the case study from it; if the same deal, align product, asset and amount across both pages.

findings.title: £120m+ holds only when EUR and USD deals are converted; a mine disposal sits in a real estate track record
findings.evidence: deals.json sums: 16 GBP deals £108.0m, 5 EUR deals 37.1m euro, 1 USD deal $3.8m. GBP equivalent about £142m to £144m at 0.84 to 0.90 GBP per euro and 0.75 to 0.80 GBP per dollar; about £127m to £129m without the Tirana 16m euro Disposal of a Chrome Ore Mine to an Asian Conglomerate, which is not real estate financing although /about-us says over £120m in real estate financing. GBP-only total is £108.0m, below £120m.
findings.recommendation: On /about-us say over £120m equivalent of real estate financing across the UK, Europe and North America. Decide whether the Tirana disposal belongs in a real estate track record; if kept, label it Corporate disposal so the 22 cards read as one set.

findings.title: Label wording differs between the live cards and deals.json (and so the concepts)
findings.evidence: Dublin: live Residential - 52 Apartments (hyphen) vs deals.json Residential – 52 Apartments (en dash, as all other cards). Metric labels: live 8.5% p.a. vs deals.json label Rate p.a. (concept F strips Rate in its terms() function; concepts D and E print Rate p.a. as a dt). London and Bath: live 11% p.a. blended vs concept 11% blended p.a. Rates per month: live 1.00% pcm vs deals.json label Rate pcm. Liverpool: SONIA + 4.15% with label Rate. Tirana: live 100% cash │ No deferred consideration vs deals.json [100%, Cash], [None, Deferred consideration], which would render None Deferred consideration if that deal were ever featured.
findings.recommendation: Normalise deals.json metric labels to the live wording (p.a., blended p.a., pcm, and for Tirana 100% cash, no deferred consideration) so every concept renders the same text as /track-record, and fix the Dublin hyphen in the Designer.

findings.title: Change direction is carried by the sign alone and the explanations live in title tooltips
findings.evidence: Rendered section: -0.25%, +0.25% and +0.025% are the same grey as the values (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-sonar/6b47e843-950d-5a6c-8dda-ec854c8993c6/scratchpad/shots/data-rates/live-rates-section.png); the script adds up/down/flat classes but no colour or icon follows. The explanations are title attributes, which touch devices never show and screen readers announce inconsistently.
findings.recommendation: Polish for the approved panel: the chip text (Held, Down 2.0 bps) already carries the meaning, so keep it as real text, not a tooltip; add a visually hidden span such as down 2.0 basis points on the previous fixing where only an icon is shown.

findings.title: Euribor arrives one to two days late from a fragile HTML scrape
findings.evidence: Feed history: the 29 Oct fixing first appeared at 13:36 UTC on 30 Oct; at 01:04 UTC on 31 Oct the 30 Oct fixing was still absent. fetch_rates.py reads the euribor-rates.eu English page with a regex over <tr> cells and assumes month/day/year dates; any template change breaks it. euribor-rates.eu itself credits EMMI and reserves rights (https://www.euribor-rates.eu/disclaimer.asp). README says the job runs twice a day while the workflow runs every 3 hours at :47.
findings.recommendation: If Euribor stays (see DR-01), read a structured source: euriborday.com reports that the Deutsche Bundesbank is an authorised distributor publishing each fixing the next business day via its time-series database (dataflow BBIG1), which offers CSV downloads; record published_at and as_of separately. If the ECB deposit facility rate replaces it, read the ECB Data Portal key-rates series. Update the README cadence sentence.

opportunities.title: Version 2 of rates.json that carries the panel's copy
opportunities.description: Add schema_version 2 with per-rate move_display, move_note, last_decision_date, last_decision_outcome, next_decision_date, previous_value, previous_as_of and attribution strings, keeping today's fields for the current footer script. The Webflow panel then only prints strings, and a Next decision 5 Nov 2026 line becomes possible without new code on the site.

opportunities.title: Swap Euribor for the ECB deposit facility rate
opportunities.description: If Clemente prefers not to license Euribor, the ECB deposit facility rate is the natural third policy rate (ECB reuse policy allows reproduction with attribution) and gives all three cards the same Held or Cut or Raised grammar and decision dates.

opportunities.title: Add the Manchester £2.665m bridging loan as a 23rd card
opportunities.description: It is the only transaction with a published case study; a card linking to the Insights post turns the track record into evidence rather than a list, and resolves the mismatch in DR-11.

opportunities.title: Print source attributions under the rates panel
opportunities.description: Source: Bank of England (Open Government Licence v3.0); Federal Reserve Board via FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; and the EMMI notice if Euribor stays. Attribution is a condition of the OGL and of FRED's terms and costs one line of small text.

## 4. Feed assessment

**Change semantics vs the approved panel.** The feed's change is the size of the last change (BoE: the 18 Dec 2025 cut; Fed: the 16/17 Sep 2026 rise) and, for Euribor, the move on the previous fixing. The approved odometer panel labels the latest decision (Held, 17 Sep 2026 decision) and the latest fixing (Down 2.0 bps, 27 Oct 2026 fixing). These are different facts. The feed has no field that says when the latest decision was or what it was, so a panel driven by today's feed could truthfully show only Cut 25 bps, 18 Dec 2025 and Raised 25 bps, 17 Sep 2026, and for Euribor it would have to infer the previous fixing's date because changed_on equals as_of.

**Fields the feed would need** (per rate, additive, keep the current fields for the live footer script):
- `as_of`: date of the data point (BoE: date of the latest Bank Rate row, not today); `published_at` for Euribor.
- `previous_value`, `previous_as_of`, `change_bps` (integer basis points, 25, -25, 2.5 for Euribor can stay decimal).
- `last_change_on`, `last_change_bps` (today's changed_on and change).
- `last_decision_date`, `last_decision_outcome` (held | cut | raised), `next_decision_date`.
- `move_display` (Held, Cut 25 bps, Raised 25 bps, Down 2.0 bps, Up 2.5 bps, Unchanged) and `move_note` (17 Sep 2026 decision, 27 Oct 2026 fixing) so the website prints strings and never derives copy.
- `attribution` string per rate; top-level `schema_version`, `checked` (already present) and `updated_display` renamed in meaning to checked.

Example (BoE, as it should read on 31 Oct 2026): value 3.75, display 3.75%, as_of 2026-10-30, previous_value 4.00, last_change_on 2025-12-18, last_change_bps -25, last_decision_date 2026-09-17, last_decision_outcome held, next_decision_date 2026-11-05, move_display Held, move_note 17 Sep 2026 decision, attribution Source: Bank of England, Open Government Licence v3.0. After 5 Nov 2026 the panel would read Held, 5 Nov 2026 decision (or Raised 25 bps, 5 Nov 2026 decision) with no site change.

**How to get decision dates without a paid source.** Keep a `calendar.json` in the repo with the published MPC dates (bankofengland.co.uk, Monetary Policy Committee dates) and FOMC dates (federalreserve.gov, FOMC meeting calendars) for the current and following year; the script sets last_decision_date to the most recent date not after today, outcome held if last_change_on is earlier than that date, else cut or raised by sign. Add a yearly GitHub issue reminder to extend the calendar. For Euribor, previous_as_of is simply the prior row of the table.

**Robustness.** Validate FRED's CSV header, numeric ranges (0 to 25) and ISO dates and raise on failure so the existing stale fallback is used (would have prevented the 400% incident). The site script should also refuse to print a value outside 0 to 25 and should honour `stale`.

**Licensing summary.**
- EMMI (Euribor administrator): delayed rates viewable free after registration with a 24-hour delay and a rolling 25-publication-day window, solely for non-commercial purposes; subscription mandatory for any commercial use (https://www.emmi-benchmarks.eu/benchmarks/euribor/rate/, https://www.emmi-benchmarks.eu/faq/subscriptions/). Delayed Data licence for website publication, 1,060 euro per hosted website per year in the 2021-2022 schedule (https://www.emmi-benchmarks.eu/globalassets/documents/pdf/communication/news/d0344a-2021-2022-fee-schedule.pdf); 2024-2025 schedule requires a licence to distribute delayed data (https://www.emmi-benchmarks.eu/globalassets/documents/pdf/subscriptions/d0196b-2024-2025-fee-schedule.pdf); 2026-2027 schedule not readable from this session (https://www.emmi-benchmarks.eu/globalassets/documents/pdf/subscriptions/d0167a-2026---2027-fee-schedule.pdf). euribor-rates.eu (Triami Media B.V.) credits EMMI and reserves all rights (https://www.euribor-rates.eu/disclaimer.asp); its sister site global-rates.com requires written permission for reproduction beyond personal use (https://www.global-rates.com/en/disclaimer/). The feed's README already records that EMMI says redisplay on a commercial site needs a licence.
- Bank of England: reproduction of data in the Bank's Database is subject to the UK Open Government Licence v3.0; the Bank holds copyright in site content; a specific attribution statement is prescribed for SONIA only (https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/legal). Bank Rate display is permitted with OGL attribution, for example Source: Bank of England, Open Government Licence v3.0.
- FRED: attribution required for any FRED content; third-party copyrighted series need the owner's permission for commercial redistribution; no implied endorsement by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/legal/, https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html). DFEDTARU and DFEDTARL are Board of Governors data (a US government work), so attribution to the Board via FRED is enough.

**Minimal concrete changes to propose for the feed repo (recommendations only, nothing was changed):**
1. fetch_rates.py: validate FRED header and all values and dates; raise to trigger the stale path.
2. fetch_rates.py: set boe.as_of to the latest Bank Rate row date; add previous_value, previous_as_of, change_bps for all three; rename semantics of changed_on to last_change_on (keep changed_on as an alias for the live script).
3. Add calendar.json (MPC and FOMC dates 2026 and 2027) and compute last_decision_date, last_decision_outcome, next_decision_date, move_display, move_note.
4. Add attribution strings and schema_version 2; add `checked_display`.
5. Euribor: move to a structured source (Bundesbank time series, published next business day, or ECB Data Portal) or switch the third rate to the ECB deposit facility rate once Clemente decides on licensing.
6. README: correct twice a day to every three hours; add the licensing decision once taken.
7. Webflow footer script: honour stale, refuse out-of-range values, show Checked rather than Updated, print attribution line.
